summary: This program stores a Celsius temperature, hands it to a small function that converts it to Fahrenheit, and prints both values in one sentence. It shows how a named function can hold a formula that the rest of the program simply calls.

lines.text: The class name describes the job the file does, and it must match the file name TemperatureConverter.java.
This is the entry point Java looks for when the program starts; everything the program does begins here.
The starting temperature is stored as a double so fractional degrees would work just as well as whole ones.
The call passes the Celsius value into the function and stores the value it hands back, keeping the conversion formula out of main.
Joining numbers to text with + turns each number into its printed form, producing one readable sentence for the traveler.
The function declares that it accepts one double and returns a double; static means it can be called directly from main without creating an object.
This is the standard conversion formula, and it is safe here because celsius is a double: the multiplication happens first, so the division by 5 keeps its decimal part instead of truncating.
